source_refs.note: Meta Directing (Deactivating) Groups: a main subheading of 20.4 Orientation in Electrophilic Substitution Reactions, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 68-69.

blocks.text: Group that makes the ring less reactive than benzene, and directs the incoming electrophile to attack on meta position only is called as-meta director. Such groups are mostly electron-withdrawing groups, that destabilize the arenium intermediate. These substituents direct the reaction to give primarily the “meta” (1,3) product.

blocks.alt: Nitrobenzene, with Cl2 over the arrow and AlCl3 under it, gives meta-chloronitrobenzene, the Cl on the carbon meta to NO2.
blocks.caption: Chlorination of nitrobenzene (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 69).

blocks.text: Major product formed in this case is meta substituted. Examples of meta– directors include -CN, C=O, -NO₂, -CO₂-. Nitrobenzene contains a meta directing group (-NO₂), its chlorination occurs at the meta position.

blocks.prompt: a) Explain why phenol can be nitrated using milder conditions than for benzene.
blocks.explanation: The oxygen of the OH group donates its lone pair to the ring and makes the ring much more reactive, so dilute nitric acid at room temperature is enough.

blocks.prompt: b) How would you prepare 3-chloronitrobenzene from benzene?
blocks.explanation: First nitrate benzene (conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄, below about 50 °C) to give nitrobenzene; then chlorinate with Cl₂ and AlCl₃ (or FeCl₃). The NO₂ group directs chlorine to the meta position. If chlorination were done first, the nitro group would go to position 2 or 4.

blocks.prompt:
c) Which products are expected to form in majority when the following are nitrated with conc. sulphuric acid and nitic acid? Give reactions
i. benzaldehyde
ii. chlorobenzene
iii. phenol
iv. Benzene carboxylic acid
blocks.explanation:
i. Benzaldehyde: CHO is a meta director → 3-nitrobenzaldehyde.
C₆H₅CHO + HNO₃ → 3-O₂NC₆H₄CHO + H₂O
ii. Chlorobenzene: Cl is an ortho-para director → 2- and 4-chloronitrobenzene (mainly 4).
C₆H₅Cl + HNO₃ → 2- and 4-ClC₆H₄NO₂ + H₂O
iii. Phenol: OH makes the ring very reactive; with conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄, NO₂ goes on all three positions (2, 4, 6) → 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid). (Dilute HNO₃ gives 2- and 4-nitrophenol.)
C₆H₅OH + 3HNO₃ → C₆H₂(NO₂)₃OH + 3H₂O
iv. Benzene carboxylic acid: COOH is a meta director → 3-nitrobenzoic acid.
C₆H₅COOH + HNO₃ → 3-O₂NC₆H₄COOH + H₂O
